2026 unit deck. Derived from slides/2023-course/lecture-02-linear-models.md, which is the faithful Marp conversion of the Fall 2023 Google Slides deck (43 slides): https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/154hDeeU5Dd5F24jP1lGyUEKfackF6REPLAuirdF_rgg/edit Changes made in this 2026 pass (2026-08-22): DROPPED - 2023 slide 2, the Acceleration Consortium screenshot (no longer relevant). - 2023 slide 20, Fall 2023 logistics (HW1 deadline, office hours) — stale, no content. ADDED — two current examples of linear models beating much larger models, placed in the Examples section right after the Sugiki cofactor slide, which already sets up one-hot encoding of protein sequences: - Virtual cell / perturbation prediction (Ahlmann-Eltze, Huber & Anders, Nature Methods 2025, plus the Arc Virtual Cell Challenge result). - Protein fitness prediction (FLIP2, Didi et al., ICML 2026). ADDED 2026-08-23 (second pass): "The everyday version: freeze the embedding, fit a linear model" — the linear-probe workflow, cited to Tang, Somia, Yu & Koo, Genome Biology 26:203 (2025). Placed after "Why does this keep happening?" so the two benchmark results land first. Cuttable if the session runs long, like the "Why does this keep happening?" slide before it. The Sugiki cofactor slide was deliberately kept: it is literally the lecture (one-hot + logistic regression + CV) and the FLIP2 slide calls back to it by name. FIXED — the 2023 conversion note deferred these to "the 2026 pass"; this is that pass: - The likelihood on the maximum-likelihood slide was written (1-p̂)^(1-y_i), missing its (x_i) argument. Now (1-p̂(x_i))^(1-y_i). The mismatched bracket P{Y_i = y_i) is also fixed. - 2023 slides 36 and 37 had their titles and figures crossed. Untangled here: the amino-acid structure diagram now sits under "Amino Acids", and the peptide-bond / chain figure under "We put amino acids together to make a protein". ALSO CORRECTED (found by re-running the Colab notebook, 2026-08-22): - The minimizer of the 0-1 training loss on the notebook's w2 grid is w2 = 1.2, not the 1.25 printed on the 2023 slides. (1.2 and 1.225 tie at a training loss of 0.25.) Both slides that quoted 1.25 now say 1.2, matching what the notebook prints. - The sklearn snippet used LogisticRegression(penalty=None). `penalty` was deprecated in scikit-learn 1.8 and is removed in 1.10. Replaced with C=np.inf, which turns regularization off the currently-supported way and gives bit-identical coefficients (verified: [-3.88912797, 4.1678537] either way). The notebook was updated to match. FIGURE REGENERATED — "How much data do we need?" (s29-loocv-vs-n.png). The notebook cell that builds the 1000-row df2 wrote df2['y'] = bernoulli(logistic(5*(-df.x1 + df.x2)), rng) using df, the earlier 100-row frame, instead of df2. Pandas aligned on index, so df2.y was NaN past row 99; it never errored only because the sweep stops at n=95. The effect was that df2's six features were mostly unrelated to its labels, which makes this slide's own caption ("data is generated using only 2 of them") false for the code that drew the figure. Fixed to df2.x1/df2.x2, and the figure regenerated from the corrected notebook. The sweep now starts at n=25 rather than n=20: with 20 points and 6 features the unregularized fit separates the data perfectly, so the held-out log loss is infinite. The 2023 figure is kept as s29-loocv-vs-n-2023.png if you want the old one back — the corrected curve is flatter (hard loss 0.40 → 0.23 instead of 0.85 → 0.35) because the labels are now actually predictable from the features. Images moved from images/lecture-02/ to images/ to match the other 2026 unit decks. The 2023 sklearn screenshot (s17-sklearn-code.png) is dropped — the code is a real block here.
